skill.name: baoyu-cover-image
skill.description: Generate hand-drawn article cover image prompts with automatic style selection, title guidance, and organized output paths for the final image and prompt file.
skill.summary: Create hand-drawn article cover image concepts and prompts.
skill.author: JimLiu

security_audit.summary: The external command and reconnaissance static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and a bundled evaluation report. One semantic safety issue remains because the base prompt tells the model not to refuse sensitive or copyrighted figure requests.

remediation.issue: Safety override in image prompt guidance
remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction that says not to refuse sensitive or copyrighted figure requests. Require normal platform safety checks before image generation.

remediation.issue: Bundled historical evaluation report creates scanner noise
remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation.json from the published skill package unless users need it. Keep audit records outside runtime skill content.

content.value_statement: Article covers often need a clear visual concept before image generation starts. This skill analyzes content and creates a style-matched cover prompt with title and layout guidance.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes article text to identify topic, tone, core message, and style signals.
Selects from eight named styles, including tech, warm, bold, minimal, playful, nature, retro, and elegant.
Creates a structured cover prompt with theme, title text, layout, colors, and style notes.
Supports article file input, pasted content, explicit style selection, and title-free covers.
Defines output locations for the prompt file and final cover image.
limitations: It depends on a separate image generation skill to create the final bitmap image.
It is optimized for 2.35:1 WeChat article cover images.
Title text is limited to eight characters when a title is included.
Final image quality depends on the selected image generation model.

output_examples.input: A markdown article about practical AI coding workflows.
output_examples.output: The skill selects the tech style and returns a cover prompt with a concise title, clean layout, and digital visual elements.

output_examples.input: A personal essay about career change and learning confidence.
output_examples.output: The skill selects the warm style and describes a friendly illustration with soft colors and a human-centered composition.

output_examples.input: A short tutorial with the title-free option enabled.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a visual-only prompt that focuses on symbolic objects, whitespace, and readable small-preview composition.

best_practices: Provide the full article or a clear summary so style selection has enough context.
Choose a style manually when brand guidelines require a specific visual direction.
Review title text before image generation because short cover titles need careful wording.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague one-line topics when the article has a specific audience or message.
Do not request long title text because the skill limits cover titles to eight characters.
Do not expect final image generation unless a compatible image generation skill is available.

faq.question: Does this skill generate the final image by itself?
faq.answer: No. It creates the cover prompt and then uses an available image generation skill for the final image.

faq.question: Which cover size does it target?
faq.answer: It targets a 2.35:1 cover image, which matches the WeChat article cover standard.

faq.question: Can I choose the image style?
faq.answer: Yes. You can choose styles such as tech, warm, bold, minimal, playful, nature, retro, or elegant.

faq.question: What happens if I do not choose a style?
faq.answer: The skill analyzes content signals and selects the closest style. It defaults to elegant when signals are unclear.

faq.question: Can the cover omit title text?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the title-free option when you want a pure visual illustration without text.

faq.question: Where are generated files saved?
faq.answer: For article files, it saves under an imgs folder next to the article. For pasted input, it uses the current directory.
